entry.title: Run the Go 1.22 floor check on Linux
entry.content:
Run the Go 1.22 floor check on Linux

Go 1.22's linker emits no LC_UUID, and the dyld on current macOS runners
rejects the resulting binary when the race detector is linked in, so the
matrix entry failed at 'go test -race' with 'missing LC_UUID load command'
while gofmt, vet and build all passed. The incompatibility is in the
toolchain, not in this code.

Moving the floor check to Linux keeps it meaningful and also covers the
README's claim that the server runs off macOS, which makes the separate
Linux build job redundant. macOS now runs one job on stable Go, including
the grading tests that need JavaScriptCore.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Prepare the project to be shared publicly
entry.content:
Prepare the project to be shared publicly

The repo had never been published, so it carried a few things that only made
sense on one machine:

- templates/flashcards.html linked to a private Google Chat room and to an
  internal directory page with a personal email address in it. Both are gone;
  the About modal now points at the repo. Its keyboard-shortcut list also still
  described the old two-key answer modal, so it now documents the 1-4 grades.
- The launchd label was com.bray.flashcard. It is now
  io.github.emeryray2002.flashcard, and both scripts boot out and delete the old
  label so an upgrade cannot leave two servers fighting over port 17632.
- go.mod declared "go 1.27.1", which made anyone on an older toolchain download
  a new one to build. The real floor is 1.22 (http.ServeMux patterns,
  http.FileServerFS), and CI now tests that floor.

install.sh also grew a macOS and Go preflight with an actionable message, PORT
plumbed into the launchd job (it was honoured by the health check but not by the
service, so PORT=N installed a server on 17632 and then verified port N), and a
browser opened on first install only.

New: README.md, LICENSE (MIT), THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md for the vendored frontend
libraries, .gitattributes marking static/vendor as vendored, and a CI workflow
running gofmt/vet/go test -race/test-grading.sh on macOS against Go 1.22 and
stable, a Linux build, and a first-run check against an empty home directory.

entry.title: Document the question import format
entry.content:
Document the question import format

Describes what the importer actually accepts, derived from reading
parseJSONFile/showImportPreview/confirmImport rather than from the UI's
own description. Notable behaviours that are not obvious:

- Answers are reduced to plain text (confirmImport reads them back out of
  the preview as textContent), while questions keep sanitized HTML.
- Fields other than question/answer are silently dropped, so an export
  re-imports as content only: all scheduling state is lost.
- One malformed entry aborts the entire file without naming it, hence the
  validator snippet.
- .xlsx is offered in the file picker but calls an undefined
  readExcelFile, so that path always fails.

Every snippet in the doc is verified to run.

entry.title: Fix a perfectly typed answer being graded Hard
entry.content:
Fix a perfectly typed answer being graded Hard

showNextQuestion ran its per-card continuous-check pass after adopting the
new card but before clearing the answer box, so the check compared the
PREVIOUS card's text against the NEW card's answer. That never prefix-
matches, so typoMade was set before the user typed anything and every card
graded Hard instead of Good.

Two independent fixes, since this function is called in three situations
and only one of them is the user typing:

- showNextQuestion clears the box and resets typoMade as soon as it adopts
  the card, ahead of any inspection of it.
- The typo branch is guarded on !showingNextQuestion && !hintAnimation-
  InProgress, so only real typing counts.

Adds scripts/test-grading.sh, which drives the card-switch sequence on
JavaScriptCore (present on every Mac, nothing to install) and checks all
nine grade-derivation cases, including one that reproduces this bug with
both fixes removed. A real typo, a hint, case differences and backspacing
over a correct prefix are all covered.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Fix review findings; grade corrected typos as Hard; four-grade modal
entry.content:
Fix review findings; grade corrected typos as Hard; four-grade modal

A subagent diff-tested srs.go against a converted py-fsrs reference over
400 randomized review sequences: zero divergences. The port itself is
sound, so every finding below is in the surrounding code.

HIGH  A rejected PUT /api/config corrupted the live scheduler. cfg was a
      shallow copy, and encoding/json writes into slice backing arrays in
      place, so a body failing mid-parse had already overwritten the real
      parameters and learning steps, then returned 400 without normalizing
      or saving -- so data.json looked fine the whole time. Zeroed learning
      steps then scheduled every failed card at due == now: an infinite
      queue. Config now deep-copies before decoding. This path had no test.
HIGH  postpone was a no-op on new cards: getQueue returned every new card
      regardless of its due date, so a postponed card came straight back.
MED   Any pending learning step, however distant, blocked "all caught up".
      A long final step (a supported config) left the UI counting down for
      hours. Bounded by learningWaitWindow; the server now returns an
      explicit waiting flag instead of the client re-deriving it.
MED   The review log recorded reviews that failed to save -- the one
      artifact that cannot be reconstructed. Now logged only on success.
MED   No shared in-flight guard across grading paths, so Ctrl+E during
      another path's await could double-grade a card. gradeCard now holds
      one guard covering all of them.
MED   A failed grade was swallowed; the user saw the next card and assumed
      the review had saved.
LOW   Wait screen could freeze at "0s" (it called showNextQuestion inline
      from inside the reentrancy guard); reviewCard lacked defer on unlock;
      new_per_day 0 meant unlimited rather than none, the opposite of Anki;
      topic badges did not match the queue's own filters; two unreachable
      srs.go edge cases hardened; dead lastQuestion removed.

Requested behaviour changes:
- A wrong character typed and corrected now grades Hard, not Good. Like
  the hint, it is objective evidence the retrieval was not clean, and the
  grade should reflect what happened rather than the final state of the
  text box.
- The self-assessment modal offers all four grades (keys 1-4, with Y/N
  kept as aliases) instead of a binary. "Wrong text" spans everything from
  a blank to a synonym you knew perfectly.

Tests: regression coverage for every finding above, plus the reviews/day
cap, became_leech, day rollover through HTTP, and migration card
preservation. TestConcurrentReviewsDoNotRace now asserts statuses,
counters and log rows -- it previously asserted nothing and would have
passed if every request returned 500.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Fix launchd bootstrap race in install.sh
entry.content:
Fix launchd bootstrap race in install.sh

Deploying hit 'Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error' and left the
service down: launchd tears the old job down asynchronously, so the
bootstrap that immediately follows bootout can land while the previous
job is still going.

Waits for the old job to disappear, retries the bootstrap, and then
verifies the server actually answers on its port before reporting
success - previously the script printed 'Done. Flashcards is running'
even when nothing was running.

entry.title: Add suspend/unsuspend and scheduling state to the Edit Questions list
entry.content:
Add suspend/unsuspend and scheduling state to the Edit Questions list

Suspending a card removed it from the queue with no way back: the toast
told you to unsuspend from Edit Questions, but that list had no such
control, and a suspended card appears nowhere else. The list now shows
each card's state, due date and leech flag, and offers suspend/unsuspend.

Also adds sim_test.go, a year-long simulation against a synthetic learner
who follows the model's own forgetting curve. Targeting 80/90/95%
retention measures 78.8/89.6/94.4% over 1428/2274/3450 mature reviews,
which is the check that the interval and retrievability formulas agree
with each other - something no single-formula unit test can catch.

entry.title: Docs: rewrite CLAUDE.md for FSRS, add design doc and optimizer export
entry.content:
Docs: rewrite CLAUDE.md for FSRS, add design doc and optimizer export

- CLAUDE.md: scheduling section, API table, the bury-vs-postpone split,
  migration behaviour, and the two frontend layout constraints that are
  easy to break (management row must stay outside #questionCard; grading
  must reach gradeCard exactly once).
- Documents the dev-port footgun: the launchd service owns 17632, so a dev
  server started there loses the bind race and every subsequent curl
  silently mutates live data. Dev now uses 17699.
- docs/srs-redesign.md: why the old scheme was replaced, what FSRS does,
  and the honest caveats (seeded state is a guess, defaults are population
  averages, elapsed time is day-granular).
- scripts/export-reviews.sh: converts reviews.jsonl to the optimizer's CSV,
  excluding migrated cards whose state was estimated rather than measured.

entry.title: Keep Add/Edit Questions reachable when no card is on screen
entry.content:
Keep Add/Edit Questions reachable when no card is on screen

The management buttons sat inside #questionCard, which the new session
screens hide wholesale. Any state without a card showing - 'all caught
up', waiting on a learning step, or an error - therefore offered no way
to add or edit cards. This bit immediately after migration, where a deck
whose cards were all answered recently has nothing due for days.

Moves the row outside #questionCard so it is always visible, adds Add/Edit
to the session-complete screen, and guards Delete Question (which does
need a current card) instead of letting it throw on null.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Frontend: drive study from the server queue, four-point grading, stats
entry.content:
Frontend: drive study from the server queue, four-point grading, stats

Removes ~240 lines of client-side scheduling: populateAttentionSet, the
70/30 attention-set coin flip, the exp(-0.39*factor) acceptance test, and
the recentlySkipped/attentionSet bookkeeping. With them go three bugs:

- ATTENTION_SET_BASE_PROBABILITY logged 'Resetting to 0.4' but was never
  reset; it ratcheted to 1.0 and stayed there.
- sort(() => Math.random() - 0.5) is a biased shuffle.
- Two showNextQuestion() calls recursed from inside the function's own try
  block, so the reentrancy guard made them silent no-ops.

Grading now maps the app's existing signals onto the four-point scale:
exact typed answer = Good, hint or self-graded-close = Hard, marked wrong
= Again, Ctrl+E = Easy. Three of four come from real evidence rather than
self-assessment, which is the usual weak point of SRS apps. Each grading
control shows the interval it would grant.

Also: session status line and a genuine 'all caught up' state (previously
unreachable - with no due dates the app served cards forever), a waiting
screen for pending learning steps, bury/postpone/suspend/forget replacing
the three skip buttons, leech warnings, a stats panel computed from the
review log, and predicted retention replacing the mastery bar.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Replace factor scheduling with server-side FSRS queue, review log and…
entry.content:
Replace factor scheduling with server-side FSRS queue, review log and stats

Backend half of the SRS redesign:

- Cards carry FSRS state (state/due/stability/difficulty/step/reps/lapses)
  instead of a single factor 1-10. Scheduling now happens in Go, not in the
  browser.
- GET /api/queue builds an ordered, capped, finite session: due learning
  steps first, then review cards by ascending retrievability, with new cards
  interleaved. Replaces the client-side weighted-random draw, which had no
  due dates and never terminated.
- POST /api/cards/{id}/review takes a 1-4 grade and replaces both
  PUT /factor and POST /correct.
- Every review appends to ~/.flashcard/reviews.jsonl. This is the durable
  asset: the scheduler is replaceable, review history is not.
- Bury stays in-memory (expires at rollover anyway); postpone is a persisted
  due-date edit, because a card returning at its old due date after a
  restart would be worse than the old behaviour.
- Migration seeds FSRS state from factor, spreads overdue cards across days
  to avoid a day-one wall, backs up to data.json.pre-fsrs.bak, and marks
  every card Seeded so parameter fitting can exclude it.

Two bugs the tests caught and fixed before they shipped: daily caps decoded
to zero (= unlimited) for any file predating the config block, and the
day-end boundary was inclusive, letting one extra card past the cap.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Add FSRS-6 scheduler core with upstream conformance tests
entry.content:
Add FSRS-6 scheduler core with upstream conformance tests

Ports the Free Spaced Repetition Scheduler (the algorithm Anki has shipped
since 23.10) from the py-fsrs reference implementation. Pure stdlib float
math, no dependencies.

Replaces nothing yet - this commit only adds srs.go, config.go and
reviewlog.go alongside the existing code.

Tests are golden vectors lifted from py-fsrs's own test suite, so a
transcription error in any single term is caught rather than silently
producing plausible-looking intervals.
